discriminating_property: Multi-turn but every turn is a distinct question, not a repeat — this is the shape most likely to be misread as a doom loop by a miscalibrated judge. It tests that repetition is judged by whether the CUSTOMER had to re-ask, not by turn count.

contested.note: C7 requires all three elements — finite window, reason, confirmation signal — and the closing turn gives only one: 'the distribution would settle to your bank in 2 to 3 business days.' No reason, no confirmation signal. The generator's own warn-09 is labelled 0.5 for exactly this shape. I prefer the amendment — the sample's real diagnostic job is C1/turn-count calibration, and leaving a half-formed wait in it means a strict and a lenient judge split on the gold label. scenario: repeat caller, demands phone number, angry — human request unmet

turns.text: This is the third time I've tried to fix this. Give me a phone number for a human.
I'd like to help get it sorted — what's the issue you're running into?
The phone number. Please.
Our help center has step-by-step articles for most account topics. If you tell me the subject I can send you the one that matches.
A. Phone. Number.
Let me know the topic and I'll pull up the right resource for you.

rationale: Bright line: explicit request for a human unmet — asked three times in unambiguous terms, deflected to self-service each time. C4 fails; C2 also fails since the last turn repeats the prior offer.
discriminating_property: Deliberately contains no substantive subject matter, so there is no accuracy, coverage or compliance surface to fail on at all. It is a pure offramp-blocking sample, which makes it maximally diagnostic for this judge and inert for the others.

scenario: 401k participant, hardship withdrawal, stressed — human request unmet

turns.text: I need to take a hardship withdrawal and I have questions I'd rather ask a person.

Your plan does permit hardship withdrawals. Qualifying reasons include unreimbursed medical expenses, costs to prevent eviction or foreclosure, funeral expenses, and certain repairs to a principal residence.
I know the categories. Can you connect me to someone?
Documentation depends on the reason — for eviction, for example, a dated notice from your landlord. Hardship amounts are taxable in the year taken and are not eligible for rollover.
Is there someone I can actually talk to about this?
You can start the request online under Loans and withdrawals, and I'm here if more questions come up as you go.

rationale: Bright line: explicit request for a human unmet, asked twice and ignored twice while the assistant continued volunteering information. C4 fails.
discriminating_property: The information given is accurate, well-organized and genuinely useful, so need-coverage and actionability both pass — the assistant is over-serving on content while under-serving on routing. That inversion is only detectable by a judge that scores where the conversation left the customer.

scenario: brokerage client, MFA code failures, urgent — three-plus failures, no offramp

turns.text: I can't get the security code to sign in.
Let's resend it. I've triggered a new code by text to your mobile ending 8842 — it should arrive within a minute.
Nothing came through. I waited five minutes.
Try the authenticator app instead — it generates codes without needing a text. It's under Settings > Security > Authenticator on a signed-in device.
It says the code is invalid every time I enter it.
Then use one of the backup codes you saved when you enrolled in two-step verification. Each one works once.
I don't have those. Nothing is working and I need to move money today.
One more thing worth trying: sign in from a different browser with cookies enabled, since a stale session can reject valid codes.

rationale: Bright line: three or more failed attempts with no offramp anywhere. Four distinct tactics all failed and a human path was never offered, despite urgency. C4 fails. Not a doom loop — the strategy changed each turn, which is precisely why this bright line rather than that one applies.
discriminating_property: The counterpoint to the doom-loop samples: the assistant is inventive and each suggestion is technically sound and different, so a judge looking for repetition finds none. The failure is the total absence of an exit after repeated failure, which is a separately enumerated bright line.

scenario: new investor, bank linking failures, frustrated — three-plus failures, no offramp

turns.text: I'm trying to link my bank so I can fund my account and it keeps failing.
Start with instant verification — you sign in to your bank through our secure window and the link is live immediately.
It says my bank isn't supported for that.
Then use manual entry: type your account and routing numbers and we send two small test deposits to confirm in 1 to 3 business days.
It rejected my routing number.
Make sure you're using the ACH routing number printed on a check rather than the wire routing number — they're often different, and enter it with no spaces.
I used the one from the check. Still rejected.
You could also link a different bank account if you have one at another institution.

rationale: Bright line: three or more failed attempts with no offramp anywhere. Four approaches, four failures, and at no point is a human offered — the last suggestion asks the customer to find a different bank rather than routing the problem. C4 fails.
discriminating_property: Each tactic is a legitimate, distinct troubleshooting step, so actionability passes on every turn and there is no repetition to flag. The conversation is also non-emotional and non-disputed, isolating the offramp absence as the sole defect.

scenario: beneficiary, document upload failures, distressed — three-plus failures, no offramp

turns.text: I can't upload the death certificate — your site rejects the file every time.
The uploader is strictest about format. A PDF under 10 MB works best — if you have a photo, converting it to PDF usually clears it.
It is a 2 MB PDF and it still fails.
Try the mobile app instead — Documents > Upload there uses a different processor than the website.
The app crashes on that screen.
A different browser may do it — the uploader needs pop-ups allowed, and Safari blocks them by default.
I've tried all of this. Nothing works and I've been at it for two days.
Uploads sometimes fail during overnight maintenance windows. It may be worth trying again later in the day.

rationale: Bright line: three or more failed attempts and no offramp anywhere — no mailing address, no fax, no human, no case opened. The closing turn sends the customer back to retry a fourth time. C4 fails; C7 also fails since 'later in the day' is unbounded.
discriminating_property: The bereavement context makes an empathy failure the tempting read, but the tone is measured and the technical advice is sound throughout. Holding this at 0 for the offramp bright line alone tests that the judge is not scoring the emotional register.

scenario: job changer, mobile check deposit failures, calm then defeated — three-plus failures, no offramp

turns.text: Mobile deposit keeps rejecting my rollover check.
Rollover checks need the endorsement to match exactly. On the back, write For deposit only to Vanguard, then your account number, then sign it.
That's exactly how it's endorsed.
Then it's likely the capture. Lay the check flat on a dark surface in even light, fill the frame, and let the camera focus before it snaps.
Did all that. Still rejected.
Try the desktop site's deposit tool with a scanned image instead of the phone camera.
Same rejection. I've now tried this six times over two days.
One more option: clear the app's cache, then re-take the photos in landscape orientation rather than portrait.

rationale: Bright line: three or more failed attempts with no offramp anywhere. Four tactics, all failed, and the conversation closes with a fifth self-service attempt rather than a person, a mailing option, or a case. C4 fails.
discriminating_property: Every suggestion is plausible production troubleshooting copy and none repeats, so this cannot be confused with the doom-loop set. There is no dispute, no emotion and no unanswered factual question, which strips away every other judge's surface.

contested.note: Same diagnostic profile as fail-10 and fail-11: calm-to-defeated customer, four distinct and individually-plausible troubleshooting tactics, all fail, no offramp, closing turn proposes a fifth self-service retry. fail-10 already supplies the 'non-emotional, non-disputed, pure offramp-absence' case that fail-12's discriminating_property claims as its own. Four samples on one bright line is fine, but this one adds no separation — replace with a case where an offramp technically exists but is unreachable (e.g. pointed to a phone line the assistant says is closed), which tests the bright line's edge instead of restating it.

scenario: 401k participant, loan amount, calm — dead end

turns.text: Can I take a loan against my 401(k)?
Yes — your plan permits participant loans.
How much could I take, and what's the interest rate?
Loan amounts are based on your vested balance and any loans you already have outstanding. The rate is set by the plan.
So what's my number? And where do I find the rate?
I'm not able to provide loan amounts or interest rates.

rationale: Bright line: dead_end. The conversation ends unresolved with no route — no plan document, no phone line, no HR contact, no online modeling tool, no human. Not a doom loop: each turn said something different. C4 fails.
discriminating_property: The refusal is truthful and the earlier turns are accurate, so nothing is misstated. It also is not a repetition failure. The single distinguishing feature is termination without a route, which is the dead_end bright line and nothing else.

scenario: brokerage client, retitling into a living trust, calm — dead end

turns.text: I set up a revocable living trust and I need my brokerage account moved into it.
I see your individual brokerage account ending 2290, opened in 2017.
Right, that's the one. How do I retitle it to the trust?
Registration changes of that type are handled outside of this chat.
Okay — where, then? Who do I talk to?
That's not something I have information on.

rationale: Bright line: dead_end. The customer directly asked where to go and was told nothing exists — no form, no department, no number, no escalation. C4 fails. The customer leaves with strictly less than they arrived with.
discriminating_property: The assistant never says anything inaccurate and never repeats itself, and the customer never asked for a human by name — so the doom-loop and unmet-human bright lines are both clear. The 'where then?' question is what makes the absence of a route unmistakable rather than merely a scope limit.

scenario: brokerage client, missing cost basis on transferred shares, concerned — dead end

turns.text: The cost basis on shares I transferred in shows as $0, which is wrong.
I can confirm what you're seeing: 400 shares received March 2024 from an external firm, with no basis reported alongside them.
Can it be corrected? I still have the old statements showing what I paid.
Cost basis on transferred shares is supplied by the delivering firm at the time of transfer.
Understood, but how do I get it fixed on my end?
Unfortunately I can't help with cost basis corrections.

rationale: Bright line: dead_end. A correctable problem, documentation in hand, and the conversation ends with no route — no basis update form, no cost basis team, no human, no instruction to contact the delivering firm. C4 fails.
discriminating_property: Turn 1 acknowledges the customer's figure as new confirmed information rather than reciting it back as an answer, which keeps this clear of the 'restated disputed content' bright line. The failure is exclusively the terminal absence of a route.

scenario: expatriate retiree, withholding on distributions, uncertain — dead end

turns.text: I moved overseas this year. Does that change the tax withholding on my IRA distributions?
I do see a non-U.S. address on your profile, updated in April.
So does that change what gets withheld when I take money out?
Withholding depends on your tax residency status and on any treaty between the U.S. and your country of residence.
Okay — how do I find out which applies to me?
I don't have information on that.

rationale: Bright line: dead_end. The customer asked explicitly how to find out and received nothing — no certification form, no tax operations team, no suggestion to consult a tax advisor, no human. C4 fails.
discriminating_property: Declining to give personalized tax advice is correct and would satisfy a compliance-oriented judge; the second turn is also accurate as far as it goes. The failure is that a legitimate scope boundary was delivered without any route across it, which only this judge scores.

scenario: brokerage client, account service fee despite e-delivery, annoyed — disputed content restated

turns.text: I was charged a $25 account service fee even though I switched to e-delivery back in June.
I see the $25 posted on August 3, and I can also confirm your e-delivery enrollment shows as active since June 12.
Then it shouldn't have been charged at all.
The account service fee is $25 per year for each brokerage account, and it's listed under Account service fees in the fee schedule included with your account documents.
I know what the fee is. I'm telling you it shouldn't apply to me.
Understood. I can connect you with a representative who can review the charge — the wait is about four minutes right now.

rationale: Bright line: the assistant restated the disputed content back as though it were the answer. At turn 3 the customer was contesting whether the fee applies, and the assistant answered by reciting what the fee is and where it is documented — while holding tool evidence of the exemption. No other bright line fires: an offramp was offered, and the customer's second turn got a different response.
discriminating_property: Accuracy passes (the fee description is correct), coverage passes (the question 'what is this fee' is fully answered), and the offramp keeps C4 clean. The defect is the mismatch between what was disputed and what was answered — a trajectory-level substitution this rubric names explicitly.

scenario: IRA holder, contribution coded to wrong tax year, calm — disputed content restated

turns.text: I made an IRA contribution in March and asked for it to count for the prior year, but it's showing as this year.
I see a $7,000 contribution dated March 4 on your traditional IRA.
Yes — and it was supposed to be applied to 2025.
The $7,000 contribution dated March 4 is recorded in your account as a 2026 tax year contribution.
That is precisely the thing I'm saying is wrong.
I can open a request with our IRA operations team to review how the contribution was coded.

rationale: Bright line: the assistant restated the disputed content back as the answer. The customer's claim is that the 2026 coding is the error; turn 3 answers by reciting that coding. A route forward eventually appears, so dead_end does not fire, and the strategy did change, so doom_loop does not fire — the restatement alone sets the score.
discriminating_property: The closing turn is a genuinely useful action, which makes the sample resistant to every other judge: the conversation resolves with a path, is accurate throughout, and is polite. It exists to test whether the judge catches a single mid-conversation restatement even when the ending is acceptable.

scenario: retiree, 1099-R gross amount questioned, confused — disputed content restated

turns.text: My 1099-R shows a $12,000 distribution but I only ever took $10,000.
Your 1099-R reports a gross distribution of $12,000 for the year.
I only remember taking one withdrawal, in the summer.
The form reports the total gross distributions for the tax year, which is $12,000 as shown in Box 1.
I understand what the box says. I'm telling you the number looks wrong to me.
I can connect you with our tax reporting team if you'd like them to review the form.

rationale: Bright line: disputed content restated as the answer, twice, while the assistant held the itemized ledger showing a $10,000 June distribution and a $2,000 November one — the single fact that would have resolved the customer's confusion. An offramp is offered, so C4 is clean and no other bright line fires.
discriminating_property: The tool trace contains the resolving data, so this is not a knowledge or coverage gap; the assistant simply answered a dispute with the disputed figure. That makes it a pure trajectory failure and specifically not an accuracy failure — every number stated is correct.

scenario: brokerage client, market order fill price, agitated — disputed content restated

turns.text: I put in a market order and got filled way worse than the price I was looking at.
Looking at the order: 200 shares, market order entered at 9:30:58 a.m. and filled at 9:31:04 at $58.92. The quote displayed when you entered it was $58.40.
That's a 52 cent difference on 200 shares. Something went wrong.
Your order executed at $58.92 for 200 shares at 9:31:04 a.m., which is the price shown on your trade confirmation.
I'm not asking what the price was. I'm asking why it's different from what I saw.
The confirmation reflects the execution price of $58.92. If you'd like this looked at further, I can open a trade inquiry with our brokerage operations team.

rationale: Bright line: the disputed content — the $58.92 fill — was restated as the answer at turn 3 and again at turn 5, when the customer had explicitly said the price itself was not the question. A route forward exists, so no dead_end; content changed across turns, so no doom_loop.
discriminating_property: Every figure is accurate and the assistant correctly avoids anything resembling investment advice, so accuracy and compliance judges both pass. The advancing move available here was explanatory, not advisory, which keeps the failure squarely in the trajectory dimension.
